# POPCDM300 Demo

Runs a basic validation of `popcdm300()` using the same parameter settings described in the MATLAB notes.

```{r setup}
# Must be in the same folder as popcdm300.R
# If not, setwd(...) first or adjust source path.
source("popcdm300.R")
```

## Demo parameters
The first parameter set (P1) uses alpha = 2.
The second (P2) uses alpha = 1, which should produce heavier tails in Ptheta.

```{r }
# P = c(vnorm, eta1, eta2, a,   alpha, kappa, ter, st)
P1 <- c(2.5,   0.01, 0.01, 2.0,   2,    20,   0.3, 0)
P2 <- c(2.5,   0.01, 0.01, 2.0,   1,    20,   0.3, 0)
nw <- 50
h <- 2.5 / 300
tmax <- 2.5
```

```{r POPCDM-TEST-RUN!}
out1 <- popcdm300(P1, nw, h, tmax)
out2 <- popcdm300(P2, nw, h, tmax)
```

```{r Structural-sanity-checks}
cat("dim(out1$Gt): ", paste(dim(out1$Gt), collapse = " x "), "\n")
cat("length(out1$T): ", length(out1$T), "\n")
cat("length(out1$Theta): ", length(out1$Theta), "\n")
cat("length(out1$Ptheta): ", length(out1$Ptheta), "\n")
cat("length(out1$Mt): ", length(out1$Mt), "\n")
```

```{r Probability/Mass-sanity-checks}
dtheta <- 2 * pi / nw
mass_gt <- sum(out1$Gt) * dtheta * h
sum_p <- sum(out1$Ptheta)

cat("Approx total mass from Gt grid (out1): ", mass_gt, "\n")
cat("Sum of Ptheta (out1): ", sum_p, "\n")
```

```{r Compare-angular-marginals-(alpha2vs1)}
plot(out1$Theta, out1$Ptheta, type = "l", lwd = 2, col = "blue",
     xlab = "Theta (radians)", ylab = "Ptheta",
     main = "POPCDM angular distribution")
lines(out2$Theta, out2$Ptheta, lwd = 2, col = "red")
legend("topright",
       legend = c("alpha = 2", "alpha = 1"),
       col = c("blue", "red"), lwd = 2, bty = "n")
```

```{r Mean-decision-time-by-angle}
plot(out1$Theta, out1$Mt, type = "l", lwd = 2, col = "darkgreen",
     xlab = "Theta (radians)", ylab = "Mt",
     main = "Conditional mean decision time by angle")
```

```{r joint-density-matrix}
# Option A: swap axes to match matrix shape directly
image(x = out1$Theta, y = out1$T, z = out1$Gt,
      xlab = "Theta (radians)", ylab = "Time",
      main = "Joint density Gt (out1)",
      col = hcl.colors(64, "YlOrRd", rev = TRUE))
```
